symbols.name: Pi
symbols.def: \(\Pi\) maps the cohort-major vector \(((v_{g1},\ldots,v_{gT})^{\prime})_{g\in C}\) to \((v_U^{\prime},v_D^{\prime})^{\prime}\)

symbols.name: Omega
symbols.type: asymptotic covariance of stacked stratified cell means

symbols.name: J
symbols.type: Jacobian of the observed mean manifold

symbols.name: hCM
symbols.type: mean-influence coefficient of the cohort-mean PPML-imputation estimator

symbols.name: F
symbols.type: primitive covariance-loading array on untreated cells

symbols.name: Z
symbols.def: \(Z=\Pi\operatorname{col}_{g\in C}\{\mathbf 1\{G=g\}(Y_g-m_g)/p_g\}\), ordered with all cells in \(U\) followed by all cells in \(D\)

symbols.name: betaHat
symbols.def: \(\widehat\beta\) is the normalized solution of \(X^{\prime}\widehat P_U[\overline Y_U-\exp(X\widehat\beta)]=0\), with normalization \(\widehat b_1=1\)

symbols.name: muHat
symbols.def: \(\widehat\mu_{gt}=\exp(x_{gt}^{\prime}\widehat\beta)\) for every \(g\in C\) and \(1\le t\le T\)

symbols.name: SHat
symbols.type: sample cohort-mean PPML untreated information matrix

symbols.name: cHat
symbols.def: \(\widehat c=(\widehat c_{\beta}^{\prime},(p_g/\widehat B)_{(g,t)\in D}^{\prime})^{\prime}\), where \(\widehat c_{\beta}=-(\widehat A/\widehat B^2)\sum_{(g,t)\in D}p_g\widehat\mu_{gt}x_{gt}\)

symbols.name: thetaHatCM
symbols.def: \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{CM}}=\widehat A/\widehat B-1\) when \(\widehat B>0\), and \(0\) otherwise

symbols.name: xiHatMK
symbols.type: Moreau--Kastler untreated individual fixed-effects PPML fit

symbols.name: thetaHatMKInd
symbols.def: \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{MK}}^{\mathrm{ind}}=\frac{\sum_{(g,t)\in D}\sum_{i=1}^{n_g}Y_{git}}{\sum_{(g,t)\in D}\sum_{i=1}^{n_g}\widehat\mu^{\mathrm{MK}}_{git}}-1\) when the denominator is positive

symbols.name: RHat
symbols.def: \(\widehat R\) replaces each \(\mu_{gt}\) in the four signed entries of \(R\) by \(\widehat\mu_{gt}\)

symbols.name: kappaHat
symbols.def: \(\widehat\kappa_{gt}=\log\overline Y_{g1}-\log\overline Y_{gt}-\log\overline Y_{\infty 1}+\log\overline Y_{\infty t}\) for finite \(g\) and \(2\le t<g\), ordered as the columns of \(\widehat R\)

symbols.name: hCMHat
symbols.def: Set \(\widehat h_{\mathrm{CM},U}=\widehat P_UX\widehat S^{-1}\widehat c_{\beta}\) and \(\widehat h_{\mathrm{CM},gt}=p_g/\widehat B\) on \(D\)

symbols.name: hstarHat
symbols.def: \(\widehat h^{\star}=\widehat h_{\mathrm{CM}}-\widehat R\widehat K^{-1}\widehat b_{\mathrm{cyc}}\) for \(q>0\), and \(\widehat h^{\star}=\widehat h_{\mathrm{CM}}\) for \(q=0\)

symbols.name: feasHat
symbols.def: \(\mathcal E_N=\{\min_{(g,t)\in U}\overline Y_{gt}>0,\ \widehat\beta\text{ exists uniquely under }\widehat b_1=1,\ \widehat B>0,\ \widehat\Sigma_g\succ0\ \forall g,\ \widehat K\succ0\text{ if }q>0\}\)

symbols.name: thetaHatEff
symbols.def: \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{eff}}=\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{CM}}-\widehat b_{\mathrm{cyc}}^{\prime}\widehat K^{-1}\widehat\kappa\) on \(\mathcal E_N\) for \(q>0\), \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{eff}}=\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{CM}}\) on \(\mathcal E_N\) for \(q=0\), and \(0\) on \(\mathcal E_N^c\)

symbols.name: VHat
symbols.def: \(\widehat V=\widehat h^{\star\prime}\widehat\Omega\widehat h^{\star}\) on \(\mathcal E_N\) and \(1\) on \(\mathcal E_N^c\)

symbols.name: Lreal
symbols.def: \(\mathcal L(m)=\{\Sigma\in\mathcal A_{\Sigma}:\exists P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bd}},\ \mathbb E_PY=m,\ \operatorname{Var}_P(Y_g)=\Sigma_g\succ0\text{ for every }g\in C\}\)

symbols.name: x0
symbols.def: Choose \(x_0\ne0\) induced by an admissible \(\rho\) and small enough that \(\|\operatorname{Var}_{P_{\rho}}(Y)-\Sigma_0\|_{\mathcal A}<\delta_0\)

assumptions.condition: \(\{Y_{gi}:1\le i\le n_g\}\perp\!\!\!\perp\{Y_{hj}:1\le j\le n_h\}\) for \(g\ne h\)
\(\mathbb E_P[Y_{gt}(0)]=a_gb_t\) for every \(g\in C\) and \(1\le t\le T\)
\(a_g>0\) for every \(g\in C\) and \(b_t>0\) for every \(1\le t\le T\)
\(\max_{g\in C,1\le t\le T}Y_{gt}\le M_0<\infty\) almost surely

definitions.name: \(\mathcal M_4\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_4=\{(P_g)_{g\in C}:T\in\mathbb N,\ T\ge3,\ D\ne\varnothing,\ \infty\in C,\ p_g>0,\ \sum_gp_g=1,\ n_g/N\to p_g,\ Y_{gi}\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P_g,\ Y_g\perp Y_h\ (g\ne h),\ Y=Y(0)\mathbf 1_U+Y(1)\mathbf 1_D,\ Y(1)=Y(0)\text{ on }U,\ \mathbb E_PY_{gt}(0)=a_gb_t,\ a_g>0,\ b_t>0,\ b_1=1,\ \mathbb E_P\|Y_g\|_2^4<\infty,\ \Sigma_g\succ0\}\)

definitions.name: \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bd}}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bd}}=\{P\in\mathcal M_4:\max_{g\in C,1\le t\le T}Y_{gt}\le M_0<\infty\ \text{almost surely}\}\)

definitions.name: \(R\)
definitions.construction: For each non-tree edge \(e=(g,t)\), \(g<\infty\), \(2\le t<g\), let \(r_e\) have entries \(+1/\mu_{g1},-1/\mu_{gt},-1/\mu_{\infty1},+1/\mu_{\infty t}\) on \((g,1),(g,t),(\infty,1),(\infty,t)\), respectively, and zero elsewhere; \(R=(r_e:e\in U\setminus\mathcal T_0)\)

definitions.name: \(\mathcal T_P\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal T_P=\overline{\{s:P_{\varepsilon}\subset\mathcal M_4\text{ is differentiable in quadratic mean at }P\text{ with score }s,\ \mathbb E_{P_{\varepsilon}}Y=m+\varepsilon z(s)+o(\varepsilon),\ \mathbb E_{P_{\varepsilon}}Y=m_{\eta}(\eta_{\varepsilon})\}}^{L_2(P)}\)\), where \(\eta_{\varepsilon}\) is differentiable at zero

definitions.name: \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{MK}}^{\mathrm{ind}}\)
definitions.construction: Fit untreated individual-observation fixed-effects PPML by maximizing \(\sum_{g\in C}\sum_{i=1}^{n_g}\sum_{t<g}[Y_{git}(\alpha_{gi}+\lambda_t)-\exp(\alpha_{gi}+\lambda_t)]\) under \(\lambda_1=0\); predict \(\widehat\mu^{\mathrm{MK}}_{git}=\exp(\widehat\alpha^{\mathrm{MK}}_{gi}+\widehat\lambda^{\mathrm{MK}}_t)\) for treated observations and form \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{MK}}^{\mathrm{ind}}=\frac{\sum_{(g,t)\in D}\sum_iY_{git}}{\sum_{(g,t)\in D}\sum_i\widehat\mu^{\mathrm{MK}}_{git}}-1\)
inputs: equal observation weights and no covariates or offsets

definitions.name: \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{eff}}\), based on cohort-mean PPML imputation
definitions.construction: From \(\overline Y_g=n_g^{-1}\sum_iY_{gi}\), \(\widehat p_g=n_g/N\), and \(\widehat\Sigma_g=n_g^{-1}\sum_i(Y_{gi}-\overline Y_g)(Y_{gi}-\overline Y_g)^{\prime}\), compute \(\widehat\beta,\widehat\mu,\widehat A,\widehat B,\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{CM}},\widehat R,\widehat\kappa,\widehat\Omega,\widehat h_{\mathrm{CM}}\) as defined above; then set \(\widehat b_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\widehat R^{\prime}\widehat\Omega\widehat h_{\mathrm{CM}}\in\mathbb R^q\), \(\widehat K=\widehat R^{\prime}\widehat\Omega\widehat R\in\mathbb R^{q\times q}\), \(\widehat h^{\star}=\widehat h_{\mathrm{CM}}-\widehat R\widehat K^{-1}\widehat b_{\mathrm{cyc}}\), \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{eff}}=\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{CM}}-\widehat b_{\mathrm{cyc}}^{\prime}\widehat K^{-1}\widehat\kappa\), and \(\widehat V=\widehat h^{\star\prime}\widehat\Omega\widehat h^{\star}\) on \(\mathcal E_N\). For \(q=0\), all cycle objects are empty, \(\widehat h^{\star}=\widehat h_{\mathrm{CM}}\), and no correction is made; on \(\mathcal E_N^c\), use the declared total fallback \((\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{eff}},\widehat V)=(0,1)\)

definitions.name: \(P_{\rho}\)
definitions.construction: Using \(s^0_{gt}=\sqrt{\tau_0m_{gt}}\), put \(Y_g=m_g+s_g^0\odot\varepsilon_g\); for finite \(g\), assign \(\Pr_{\rho}(\varepsilon_g=e)=2^{-T}[1+\sum_{t=2}^{g-1}\rho_{gt}e_te_g]\) under \(\sum_{t=2}^{g-1}|\rho_{gt}|<1\), retain independent Rademacher coordinates for \(g=\infty\), and set \(x_{gt}=s^0_{gt}s^0_{gg}\rho_{gt}\). Complete the potential outcomes by \(Y_{gt}(0)=Y_{gt}(1)=Y_{gt}\) on \(U\), \(Y_{gt}(1)=Y_{gt}\) on \(D\), and \(Y_{gt}(0)=\mu_{gt}\) on \(D\)

definitions.name: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{tan}}\)
definitions.construction: For each cohort set \(w_g^{(L)}=(Y_g-m_g)\mathbf 1\{\|Y_g-m_g\|_2\le L\}\) and \(u_g^{(L)}=w_g^{(L)}-\mathbb E_Pw_g^{(L)}\); choose finite \(L_g\) for which \(C_g=\mathbb E_P[(Y_g-m_g)u_g^{(L_g)\prime}]\) is invertible, which exists because \(C_g\to\Sigma_g\succ0\). For \(s\in L_2^0(P)\) with \(z(s)=Jv\), truncate and center to \(s_g^{[\ell]}\), and set \(\widetilde s_g^{[\ell]}=s_g^{[\ell]}+u_g^{(L_g)\prime}C_g^{-1}[z_g(s)-z_g(s^{[\ell]})]\). With the smooth mean chart \(m_{\eta}\), define \(dP_{g,\varepsilon}^{[\ell]}/dP_g=1+\varepsilon\widetilde s_g^{[\ell]}+u_g^{(L_g)\prime}\lambda_g^{[\ell]}(\varepsilon)\), where \(\lambda_g^{[\ell]}(\varepsilon)=C_g^{-1}[m_{\eta,g}(\eta+\varepsilon v)-m_g-\varepsilon z_g(s)]\). For sufficiently small positive and negative \(\varepsilon\), this is a positive support-preserving density, has mean \(m_{\eta,g}(\eta+\varepsilon v)\), and score \(\widetilde s_g^{[\ell]}\)

definitions.name: \(\mathbb B_{\mathcal A}(\Sigma_0,\delta_0)\)
definitions.construction: For each \(\Sigma\) with \(\|\Sigma-\Sigma_0\|_{\mathcal A}<\delta_0\), let \(Y_g=m_g+\Sigma_g^{1/2}\varepsilon_g\), where \(\varepsilon_g\) has independent Rademacher coordinates. Weyl's inequality gives \(\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_g)>\lambda_0/2\), while \(\|\Sigma_g^{1/2}-\Sigma_{g0}^{1/2}\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\delta_0/\sqrt{\lambda_0}\); hence every coordinate of \(Y_g\) is at least \(d_0-\sqrt T\delta_0/\sqrt{\lambda_0}>d_0/2\), so \(\mathbb B_{\mathcal A}(\Sigma_0,\delta_0)\subset\mathcal L(m)\)

definitions.name: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{grow}}\)
definitions.construction: Analyze a spectrally regularized projection of the empirical cycle score \(\widehat\kappa\) using the eigenspaces of \(\widehat K\), with bias controlled by the discarded cycle loading \(\widehat b_{\mathrm{cyc}}\) and stochastic error controlled by a self-normalized graph-cycle central limit argument
inputs: the empirical cycle triple \((\widehat K,\widehat b_{\mathrm{cyc}},\widehat\kappa)\)
a sequence of growing untreated graphs

definitions.name: \(\mathsf E_3\)
definitions.construction: Take \(T=3\), \(C=\{2,3,\infty\}\), \(p_g=1/3\), \(a_g=1\), \(b=(1,2,3)\), and treated multiplier \(3/2\), so the observed mean rows are \((1,3,9/2),(1,2,9/2),(1,2,3)\). Cohorts \(2\) and \(\infty\) have independent coordinate noise \(\pm1/10\). Cohort \(3\) has noise \(((U_0/10+e_1/20),(-U_0/10+e_2/20),(U_0/10+e_3/20))\), where \(U_0,e_1,e_2,e_3\) are independent Rademacher variables
inputs: four independent Rademacher signs in cohort \(3\)
independent coordinate signs in cohorts \(2\) and \(\infty\)

statements.statement: Under the positive connected rank-one untreated-mean model, the weighted fundamental cycles are complete: \(\ker(J^{\prime})=\operatorname{col}(R)\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(R)=q=|U|-|C|-T+1\).
statements.justification: This identifies every locally informative mean restriction and makes the graph cycle rank the exact dimension of overidentification.
statements.gap: Király, Theran, and Tomioka (2015, Theorem 34 and Remark 35) identify rank-one circuit polynomials; they do not derive the weighted tangent restriction space for proportional staggered DiD.
statements.consumer: The result gives proportional-DiD analysts a graph-only count of all covariance-sensitive precision directions before estimation.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_4\), every \(s\in L_2^0(P)\) satisfying \(R^{\prime}z(s)=0\) is the \(L_2(P)\) limit of bounded scores of two-sided support-preserving differentiable-in-quadratic-mean submodels in \(\mathcal M_4\) whose mean paths lie exactly in the smooth chart \(m_{\eta}\); hence \(\mathcal T_P=\{s\in L_2^0(P):R^{\prime}z(s)=0\}\).
statements.justification: The bounded truncation and exact mean correction establish the reverse tangent inclusion that a derivative convention alone cannot supply.
statements.gap: Newey (1990, Sections 2--3) gives general score calculus but not this support-preserving density construction for a nonnegative rank-one cohort panel.
statements.consumer: The lemma licenses the sharp finite-fourth-moment lower bound used by every efficiency comparison in the proposal.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_4\), relative to the explicitly mean-differentiable differentiable-in-quadratic-mean experiment \(\mathcal T_P\), the canonical gradient is \(\phi^{\star}=h^{\star\prime}Z\), and every regular estimator of \(\theta_{\mathrm{PTT}}\) has asymptotic variance at least \(V^{\star}\).
statements.justification: The tangent equality converts the rank-one mean manifold into a sharp semiparametric lower bound rather than a formal generalized-method-of-moments projection.
statements.gap: Chamberlain (1987) and Newey (1990) provide projection machinery, while Moreau--Kastler (2025, Section 3.2.2) provides no tangent experiment or efficiency bound for the proportional ratio.
statements.consumer: The bound is the precision benchmark needed to assess PPML inference in the regional-trade-agreement and treaty applications.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(P\in\mathcal M_4\), on \(\mathcal E_N\) the fixed-target-weight cohort-mean PPML-imputation estimator obeys \(\sqrt N(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{CM}}-\theta_{\mathrm{PTT}})=h_{\mathrm{CM}}^{\prime}\sqrt N(\overline Y-m)+o_P(1)\), with asymptotic variance \(h_{\mathrm{CM}}^{\prime}\Omega h_{\mathrm{CM}}\).
statements.justification: This differentiates the cohort-mean comparator defined in the core and identifies the exact coefficient whose cycle projection governs its efficiency loss.
statements.gap: Moreau--Kastler (2025, Section 3.2.2, equations 3.13--3.14) instead fits untreated individual-observation fixed effects and aggregates individual counterfactual predictions; neither that paper nor Wooldridge (2023, Sections 2--3) provides this cohort-mean influence expansion under arbitrary within-unit covariance.
statements.consumer: The expansion lets analysts compute the cohort-mean estimator's variance and its distance from the canonical bound without conflating it with an individual fixed-effects procedure.

statements.statement: Suppose both normalized PPML fits exist uniquely, the panel contains one observation per unit and period, the Moreau--Kastler fit uses equal observation weights with no covariates or offsets, and \(n_g/N=p_g\) for every \(g\in C\). Profiling its individual fixed effects gives the cohort-mean PPML time-score equations and \(\sum_{i=1}^{n_g}\widehat\mu^{\mathrm{MK}}_{git}=n_g\widehat\mu_{gt}\); consequently \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{MK}}^{\mathrm{ind}}=\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{CM}}\).
statements.justification: The boundary result states the exact aggregation conditions under which the distinct individual and cohort-mean procedures coincide.
statements.gap: Moreau--Kastler (2025, Appendix B2) links individual imputation to a fully interacted individual-level estimator; it does not state this profiling identity with the cohort-mean rank-one score used here.
statements.consumer: Applied users can determine whether the cycle frontier transfers exactly to their implementation or only describes a cohort-mean benchmark.

statements.statement: The covariance-weighted cycle estimator satisfies \(\sqrt N(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{eff}}-\theta_{\mathrm{PTT}})=N^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^N\phi_i^{\star}+o_P(1)\) and attains \(V^{\star}\) pointwise over \(\mathcal M_4\).
statements.justification: Attainment turns the information bound into an implementable precision correction based only on cohort means and within-cohort covariances.
statements.gap: Roth and Sant'Anna (2023, Proposition 2.1) optimize design-based additive estimators within a class; this result attains the superpopulation semiparametric bound for a nonlinear proportional target.
statements.consumer: Applied users obtain an analytic alternative to unit-bootstrap inference for the cohort-mean PPML benchmark in fixed-horizon panels.

statements.statement: At every interior \(P\in\mathcal M_4\), \(h_{\mathrm{CM}}=h^{\star}\) if and only if \(b_{\mathrm{cyc}}=0\), equivalently \(F_{g1}-F_{gt}-F_{\infty1}+F_{\infty t}=0\) for all finite \(g\) and \(2\le t<g\); these \(q\) covariance equations are linearly independent.
statements.justification: The theorem translates efficiency of the cohort-mean PPML score into exactly \(q\) observable, primitive alternating covariance balances.
statements.gap: Ciani and Fisher (2019, printed page 7, Section 3.1) state that PPML may fail to be the most efficient estimator, and their Appendix B simulations show the efficiency loss; no prior result gives an exact covariance-law characterization indexed by untreated cycles.
statements.consumer: Researchers can diagnose whether cohort-mean PPML already exhausts the precision in their untreated panel.

statements.statement: For every fixed interior mean \(m\) with \(q>0\), the family \(P_{\rho}\) has mean \(m\), belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bd}}\), satisfies \(b_{\mathrm{cyc}}(x)=-B^{-1}D_{\mu}^{-1}x\) and \(K(x)=K_0\), and therefore obeys \(\Gamma(x)=B^{-2}x^{\prime}D_{\mu}^{-1}K_0^{-1}D_{\mu}^{-1}x>0\) for every nonzero admissible \(x\). Moreover \(\mathbb B_{\mathcal A}(\Sigma_0,\delta_0)\subset\mathcal L(m)\), and the explicitly chosen \(x_0\) and \(\eta_0\) satisfy \(\mathbb B_{\mathcal A}(\Sigma(x_0),\eta_0)\subset\mathcal L(m)\) with \(\Gamma>0\) throughout that ambient open ball.
statements.justification: Support-preserving realizability shows that strict inefficiency is robust and not an artifact of perturbing an impossible covariance matrix.
statements.gap: The rank-one completion and additive efficient-DiD literatures do not construct a legal nonnegative fixed-support family with an exact positive-definite cohort-mean PPML loss form.
statements.consumer: The family supplies calibrated stress tests and interpretable variance-loss directions for cohort-mean proportional PPML applications.

statements.statement: Fix \(m\) and \(p\). The cohort-mean PPML-imputation estimator is semiparametrically efficient for \(\theta_{\mathrm{PTT}}\) at every law \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bd}}\) satisfying \(\mathbb E_PY=m\) if and only if \(q=0\); when \(q>0\), its efficient covariance laws are exactly \(\mathcal L(m)\cap\ker(\mathcal L_m)\), where \(\mathcal L_m:\mathcal A_{\Sigma}\to\mathbb R^q\) has rank \(q\), and \(\|b_{\mathrm{cyc}}\|_2^2/\lambda_{\max}(K)\le\Gamma\le\|b_{\mathrm{cyc}}\|_2^2/\lambda_{\min}(K)\). This strictly sharpens Ciani and Fisher's printed-page-7, Section 3.1 observation and Appendix B simulation evidence that PPML may fail to be most efficient by giving necessity, sufficiency, and codimension for the stated cohort-mean estimator.
statements.justification: This is the topology-level kernel: cycles are necessary and sufficient for covariance laws on which feasible precision improvement exists.
statements.gap: Ciani and Fisher (2019, printed page 7, Section 3.1) state that PPML may fail to be the most efficient estimator, with the corresponding efficiency-loss simulations in Appendix B; Moreau--Kastler (2025, equations 3.13--3.14) and Wooldridge (2023, Sections 2--3) study distinct individual-level imputation procedures. None gives an acyclic if-and-only-if frontier or an exact codimension count for the cohort-mean rank-one estimator.
statements.consumer: The theorem tells analysts in the Nagengast--Yotov and Menkhoff--Miethe settings exactly when the transparent cohort-mean PPML benchmark is universally precision-optimal before moving to richer individual-level specifications.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(P\in\mathcal M_4\), \(\widehat V\to_PV^{\star}\), \(\sqrt N(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{eff}}-\theta_{\mathrm{PTT}})/\sqrt{\widehat V}\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1)\), and \(\Pr_P\{\theta_{\mathrm{PTT}}\in[\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{eff}}\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V/N}]\}\to1-\alpha\).
statements.justification: Pointwise studentization completes the estimator contribution without claiming unsupported uniform inference over tail-escaping laws.
statements.gap: Moreau--Kastler (2025, printed page 21) recommends a panel bootstrap, while the proposed efficient correction has no published analytic Wald theory.
statements.consumer: The result yields directly reportable confidence intervals for proportional treatment effects under arbitrary within-unit dependence.

statements.statement: If \(q=0\), then \(R\) has no columns, \(h_{\mathrm{CM}}=h^{\star}\), \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{eff}}=\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{CM}}\), and \(\Gamma=0\). Within the maintained model, the canonical acyclic support \(C=\{2,\infty\}\) has \(q=0\) for every fixed \(T\ge3\), and on \(\mathcal E_N\), \[\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{eff}}=\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{CM}}=\frac{\sum_{t=2}^T\overline Y_{2t}}{\overline Y_{21}\sum_{t=2}^T(\overline Y_{\infty t}/\overline Y_{\infty1})}-1.\]
statements.justification: The reduction checks inside the maintained \(T\ge3\) model that the cycle correction vanishes and that cohort-mean PPML becomes an explicit multi-post multiplicative ratio.
statements.gap: Ciani and Fisher (2019) establish the canonical two-period multiplicative DiD ratio; this proposition gives the admissible fixed-\(T\), \(T\ge3\), acyclic analogue that pools all post-adoption cells.
statements.consumer: Users with one treated cohort and a never-treated cohort can compute the multi-post proportional effect directly and omit covariance-cycle estimation.

statements.statement: In \(\mathsf E_3\), all realized outcomes are positive, \(q=1\), \(\theta_{\mathrm{PTT}}=1/2\), \(V^{\star}=395643/6246400\), \(\operatorname{Var}(h_{\mathrm{CM}}^{\prime}Z)=6663/102400\), and \(\Gamma=27/15616\); hence the cohort-mean PPML variance exceeds the bound by approximately \(2.73\) percent of \(V^{\star}\).
statements.justification: The exact rational witness makes the cohort-mean PPML topology loss quantitatively auditable in the smallest cyclic staggered panel.
statements.gap: Published multiplicative DiD examples do not report this PTT-specific canonical bound and exact cycle loss for a legal nonnegative covariance law.
statements.consumer: The exhibit provides a reproducible calibration for implementations of the cycle correction.

statements.statement: For a sequence with \(T\) and cycle rank \(q\) increasing, characterize the weakest graph-spectrum and moment conditions under which a feasible regularized cycle correction is asymptotically linear for \(\theta_{\mathrm{PTT}}\), attains the relevant growing-dimensional efficiency frontier, and supports valid studentization, using \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{grow}}\) as the construction handle.
statements.justification: The fixed-horizon theorem leaves open how many noisy overidentifying cycle directions can be exploited when adoption calendars lengthen.
statements.gap: Borusyak, Jaravel, and Spiess (2024, Theorems 1--2) treat additive efficient imputation at fixed design dimension and do not analyze a growing weighted cycle Gram spectrum for a proportional ratio.
statements.consumer: A solution would provide principled regularization and inference for long staggered panels with many pretreatment cycles.

sampling_model.design: Fixed \(T\), deterministic cohort strata, and known target weights \(p_g\).
sampling_model.units: Within each \(g\in C\), \(n_g\) units are independent and identically distributed; cohort samples are mutually independent and \(n_g/N\to p_g>0\).
sampling_model.treatment: The required cohort \(\infty\in C\) is never treated; each \(g<\infty\) first receives treatment at \(t=g\), and no anticipation and consistency connect observed and potential outcomes.
sampling_model.overlap: The full-panel untreated graph \(H_U\) contains the canonical spanning tree through cohort \(\infty\), is connected, and has \(D\ne\varnothing\); all cohort shares are positive.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Compute \(\overline Y_g\), \(\widehat p_g\), and \(\widehat\Sigma_g\) from each cohort; fit the normalized fixed-dimensional untreated cohort-mean PPML model, then form \(\widehat R,\widehat b_{\mathrm{cyc}},\widehat K,\widehat h^{\star}\), and \(\widehat V\) on \(\mathcal E_N\). No cross-fitting is required.

estimand_functional: \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{eff}}=\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{CM}}-\widehat b_{\mathrm{cyc}}^{\prime}\widehat K^{-1}\widehat\kappa\), \(\widehat V=\widehat h^{\star\prime}\widehat\Omega\widehat h^{\star}\), \(\phi^{\star}=h^{\star\prime}Z\), and \(\Gamma=b_{\mathrm{cyc}}^{\prime}K^{-1}b_{\mathrm{cyc}}\), with the cycle correction empty when \(q=0\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Section 3.2.2, equations 3.13--3.14 fit untreated individual-observation fixed-effects PPML, predict individual treated counterfactuals, and aggregate their ratio; printed page 21 recommends a unit panel bootstrap.

Printed page 7, Section 3.1 states that PPML may fail to be the most efficient estimator, and Appendix B reports the simulations showing the efficiency loss; Appendix C is the empirical Educational Maintenance Allowance application.
Theorem 34 identifies rank-one circuit graphs as simple even cycles and Remark 35 turns their positive-entry relations into alternating log-linear equations.
Proposition 2.1 gives covariance-dependent variance-minimizing coefficients within a design-based class of additive staggered-rollout estimators.
Theorems 3.1--3.2 derive efficient influence functions for additive DiD and event-study parameters under sequential parallel-trends moment restrictions.
Theorems 1--2 characterize efficient linear unbiased additive event-study estimation and its imputation representation under the paper's error model.

Sections 2--3 specify individual-level fully interacted nonlinear conditional means, impute individual untreated counterfactuals, and show canonical-link equality of imputation and pooled quasi-likelihood estimates of cohort--time average treatment effects.

tldr: In a fixed-horizon proportional staggered panel with the required never-treated cohort \(\infty\in C\), the untreated rank-one mean restrictions have one independent weighted tangent direction per graph cycle. A bounded truncation-and-correction construction proves tangent equality for the explicitly mean-differentiable finite-fourth-moment experiment, and the canonical gradient subtracts the covariance projection of a distinct cohort-mean PPML-imputation influence function onto those directions. This cohort-mean estimator is efficient for every bounded legal covariance law exactly when the untreated graph is acyclic; with cycle rank \(q>0\), the exceptional efficient laws satisfy exactly \(q\) primitive alternating covariance balances, while an explicit support-preserving family and a positive-radius ambient covariance ball certify strictly positive exact quadratic loss. A feasible cycle correction attains the bound and supports pointwise Wald inference. Moreau--Kastler's individual fixed-effects imputation and Wooldridge's fully interacted individual-level nonlinear imputation inform the construction but are not identified with it outside an explicit aggregation boundary.

project_justification.gap: Moreau--Kastler (2025) fits untreated individual fixed effects and aggregates individual counterfactual predictions into PTT, while Wooldridge (2023) develops fully interacted individual-level nonlinear imputation for cohort--time average treatment effects. Neither provides an efficiency frontier for the distinct cohort-mean rank-one PPML score; existing efficient staggered-DiD results are additive, and rank-one completion results do not classify causal-estimator efficiency.
project_justification.niche: The positive cohort-mean rank-one untreated manifold makes graph cycles simultaneously the overidentifying restrictions and the covariance-sensitive precision directions, permitting an exact topology-level efficiency frontier without claiming equivalence to richer individual-level counterfactual specifications.
project_justification.fill: The project proves weighted-cycle tangent completeness by a support-preserving score construction, derives and attains the canonical gradient with explicit sample covariance functionals, differentiates the cohort-mean PPML-imputation estimator, characterizes its efficient covariance laws by \(q\) primitive balances, and certifies strict loss on a realizable bounded family and a positive-radius ambient covariance neighborhood. A boundary proposition supplies the exact profiling conditions under which the Moreau--Kastler individual estimator collapses to the cohort-mean estimator.

related_work: Moreau--Kastler (2025, Section 3.2.2, equations 3.13--3.14) estimates individual fixed effects and time effects by PPML on never-treated and not-yet-treated individual observations, predicts individual untreated counterfactuals, and aggregates the treated observed-to-predicted ratio; the estimator analyzed here instead fits a cohort-mean rank-one score and is therefore only informed by that paper. The aggregation-bridge proposition isolates exact equality under equal observation weights, no covariates or offsets, balanced individual panels, and target shares equal to sample shares. Wooldridge (2023, Sections 2--3, especially equations 3.12--3.13 and the canonical-link discussion) specifies fully interacted individual-level nonlinear conditional means, obtains individual counterfactual predictions and cohort--time effects, and proves imputation--pooled quasi-likelihood equivalence; it neither uses the cohort-mean rank-one score nor targets the same aggregate ratio. Ciani and Fisher (2019, printed page 7, Section 3.1) state that PPML may fail to be the most efficient estimator, and Appendix B reports simulations showing the efficiency loss; Appendix C is instead the empirical Educational Maintenance Allowance application. The present theorem strictly sharpens that qualitative possibility for the stated cohort-mean estimator to an acyclic if-and-only-if frontier and exact codimension. Király, Theran, and Tomioka (2015, Theorem 34 and Remark 35) show that rank-one matrix circuits are even cycles; their algebraic relation informs the complete weighted tangent restriction basis. Chamberlain (1987) and Newey (1990) supply projection and tangent-score tools, but not the nonnegative support-preserving submodel construction. Roth and Sant'Anna (2023, Proposition 2.1), Borusyak, Jaravel, and Spiess (2024, Theorems 1--2), and Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie (2025, Theorems 3.1--3.2) develop covariance-aware efficiency for additive staggered DiD rather than the nonlinear PTT ratio and its graph-topological frontier. Wooldridge (1999) supplies distribution-free fixed-effects Poisson theory. Nagengast and Yotov (2025) and Menkhoff and Miethe (2019) are concrete bilateral-data consumers, although their richer dependence and fixed effects remain outside the benchmark theorem.
technical_internal_limitation: Because \(\infty\in C\) and the panel is fully observed, \(q=\sum_{g<\infty}(g-2)\); the topology theorem does not claim arbitrary missing-panel graph generality. There is no positive loss bound uniform over all inefficient laws because \(\Gamma(x)\to0\) as \(x\to0\). Singular covariance blocks, zero mean cells, random cohort shares, growing \(T\), unbalanced panels, and dyadic shared-country dependence are outside the formal model. The finite-fourth-moment tangent result is pointwise for the explicitly mean-differentiable differentiable-in-quadratic-mean experiment and uses bounded support-preserving submodels constructed by truncation and exact mean correction; it does not classify tail-escaping paths for which score-moment differentiation fails.
honest_scope: The theorem contributions concern the explicitly defined cohort-mean PPML-imputation estimator: PTT-specific weighted-cycle completeness, constructive tangent equality for the mean-differentiable finite-fourth-moment experiment, the exact rank-\(q\) primitive covariance map, the acyclic universal-efficiency equivalence, and a legal bounded family with exact quadratic loss and an ambient positive-radius strict-loss neighborhood. No general identity with Moreau--Kastler's individual fixed-effects imputation or Wooldridge's fully interacted individual-level nonlinear estimator is asserted; exact equality with the former is confined to the stated aggregation boundary. Canonical projection algebra and routine sandwich consistency are supporting machinery. The open-ended question concerns growing horizon and growing cycle rank. The admissible tree reduction uses \(C=\{2,\infty\}\) at fixed \(T\ge3\) and yields the explicit multi-post multiplicative ratio, while the exact three-period witness audits the smallest cyclic case.

seed_details.seed: Cycle-rank if-and-only-if efficiency frontier for cohort-mean PPML imputation
seed_details.anchor_locator: Introduction; Section 3.2.2, equations 3.13--3.14; printed page 21; Conclusion.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The anchor's argument fits untreated individual fixed effects and ends with probability convergence of an aggregate imputation ratio. The new analysis instead differentiates the explicitly defined cohort-mean ratio jointly with the rank-one untreated mean manifold and identifies every orthogonal tangent direction; an aggregation proposition states when the two estimators coincide.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for proportional PTT with semiparametric efficiency, PPML with graph cycle rank, and multiplicative staggered DiD with canonical gradients found no exact target--method match; ChenSantAnnaXie2025 is additive and KiralyTheranTomioka2015 is noncausal matrix completion.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Immediate from generic optimal generalized method of moments because cycles merely count overidentifying restrictions.
seed_details.rebuttal: Generic projection does not prove that every staggered cycle is PTT-relevant, that the cohort-mean covariance map has rank exactly \(q\), or that a bounded nonnegative law realizes a full strict-loss neighborhood.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The kernel is an if-and-only-if theorem plus a generic-region realizability result, not a single covariance witness or a relabeled projection identity.

seed_details.seed: Finite-fourth-moment tangent bound and feasible canonical-gradient attainment for PTT
seed_details.anchor_locator: Section 3.2.2, equations 3.13--3.14 and the unit-bootstrap sentence on printed page 21.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed proof step replaces consistency of an individual-prediction ratio with density of support-preserving scores for the cohort-mean rank-one experiment whose mean derivatives lie in the Jacobian column space.
seed_details.destination_search: Newey1990 and Chamberlain1987 give abstract score projection, while ChenSantAnnaXie2025 derives additive DiD efficient influence functions; none treats nonnegative rank-one PTT with arbitrary within-unit covariance.
seed_details.cynical_objection: A smooth finite-dimensional mean restriction makes the efficient influence function a textbook formula.
seed_details.rebuttal: The formula is routine, but tangent completeness under nonnegative support and only finite fourth moments, plus an attaining feasible estimator for the nonlinear PTT ratio, is not supplied by the textbook formula.
seed_details.selection: survived and integrated into chosen kernel
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The proposal isolates the nonroutine score-density step and does not sell the projection formula alone.

seed_details.seed: Dyadic exchangeable extension of the proportional cycle frontier
seed_details.anchor_locator: Introduction and empirical Sections 5.1--5.2 on bilateral trade and bank deposits; Conclusion.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first invalid step is the independent-strata direct-sum tangent space. It must be replaced by an Aldous--Hoover or Hoeffding projection that tracks exporter and importer components before cycle projection.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing dyadic exchangeable efficiency with proportional staggered PPML found generic multiway-cluster limit theory but no PTT canonical gradient or cycle frontier.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Generic multiway-cluster theory mechanically replaces the independent covariance matrix.
seed_details.rebuttal: Degenerate dyadic projections can change the rate and limit law, so the canonical gradient and the necessity of \(q=0\) are not obtained by a covariance substitution.
seed_details.selection: survived literature scan but not chosen because the independent-unit kernel is substantially more feasible
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed identifies the first broken proof step and a dependence-driven limit object rather than appending clustered standard errors.

seed_details.seed: Growing-cycle-rank spectral limit law for covariance-corrected proportional DiD
seed_details.anchor_locator: Theorem 34, Remark 35, Algorithm 6, and Section 8 Discussion and Outlook.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The fixed-dimensional inversion of \(K=R^{\prime}\Omega R\) is the first changed step; growing \(q\) requires spectral regularization and a joint limit for estimated cycle residuals.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for growing cycle rank with PPML DiD and spectral regularization found matrix-completion error work but no proportional causal ratio limit law.
seed_details.cynical_objection: This is a routine high-dimensional generalized-method-of-moments extension.
seed_details.rebuttal: The spectrum is constrained by a weighted graph cycle Gram matrix and estimated rank-one means, so admissible regularization and the phase transition are topology-specific.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The focal object is the cycle-Gram spectral regime, not a generic growing-parameter slogan.

seed_details.seed: Critical multiplicative-trend violation for PTT sign and estimator ranking
seed_details.anchor_locator: Introduction; Section 3.2.2 on multiplicative imputation; Conclusion.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Replace exact rank-one means by bounded log-cycle violations and first derive how the PTT identified set and the PPML-versus-efficient ranking vary with the violation radius.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for multiplicative staggered-DiD sensitivity with a critical violation radius found additive parallel-trend sensitivity but no closed-form cycle-based PTT threshold.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Log-cycle residual bounds are an immediate multiplicative rewrite of additive trend sensitivity.
seed_details.rebuttal: The target is a ratio whose denominator is jointly completed across cycles, so the sharp critical radius and covariance-aware ranking do not follow from additive bounds.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: A publishable version must derive closed-form endpoints and a named critical radius; qualitative robustness alone is rejected.

seed_details.seed: Minimax PTT estimation when the number of untreated cycles grows
seed_details.anchor_locator: Introduction; Theorems 1--2 and their proofs; Conclusion and Appendix A.7.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The anchor's fixed-horizon linear-imputation weights become an estimated nonlinear cycle correction; the first changed step is controlling the inverse cycle Gram matrix while constructing a matching local alternative.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for minimax rates of staggered proportional DiD with growing pretreatment dimension found no direct match.
seed_details.cynical_objection: The rate is determined immediately by the smallest eigenvalue of a growing information matrix.
seed_details.rebuttal: A matching converse must respect nonnegative support, staggered observation geometry, and the nonlinear denominator rather than perturb an unrestricted Gaussian sequence.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed requires both a legal estimator and a topology-respecting converse; it is not another fixed-dimensional efficiency restatement.

seed_details.seed: Finite-sample permutation inversion of weighted log-cycle residuals
seed_details.proof_boundary: The anchor's randomization group acts on assigned adoption times, whereas observational proportional DiD has no known assignment symmetry. The first changed step is to identify a valid block-exchangeability orbit for untreated cycle residuals.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing conformal or permutation inference with multiplicative staggered PPML found no exact result, but the absence of a known assignment law sharply limits scope.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Without randomized timing, the permutation distribution is invalid.
seed_details.rebuttal: The seed survives only for explicitly block-exchangeable or randomized-timing designs, where the orbit is a substantive additional design object rather than a placebo heuristic.
seed_details.selection: credible only in a narrower randomized-timing model and not shortlisted
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The restriction to a known symmetry group is explicit; no finite-sample validity is claimed for the observational benchmark.

seed_details.seed: Proportional treatment-policy regret from staggered imputed counterfactual means
seed_details.proof_boundary: The scalar PTT aggregation must be replaced first by a policy-indexed ratio value and an orthogonal covariance-weighted score before empirical welfare maximization can be analyzed.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for policy learning from multiplicative staggered DiD identified no direct target--method paper, but existing policy-learning theory makes the novelty depend on a genuinely ratio-specific regret geometry.
seed_details.cynical_objection: This merely feeds an estimated PTT into standard empirical welfare maximization.
seed_details.rebuttal: A viable theorem would need a policy-indexed counterfactual denominator, ratio-orthogonal scores, and regret controlled under cycle-dependent estimation error; without those it would be dropped.
seed_details.selection: credible research direction but not shortlisted
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed is not selected because the current evidence supports a fixed-estimand efficiency theorem more directly than a policy objective.

Wooldridge (2023, Sections 2--3, especially equations 3.12--3.13 and the canonical-link discussion) develops fully interacted individual-level nonlinear conditional means, individual counterfactual imputation, and cohort--time average treatment effects; this is not the cohort-mean rank-one estimator analyzed here. novelty_justification: The closest result sets are Moreau--Kastler (2025), whose equations 3.13--3.14 aggregate counterfactuals from an untreated individual fixed-effects PPML fit, Wooldridge (2023), whose fully interacted individual-level nonlinear specification targets cohort--time average treatment effects, and Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie (2025), which derives additive staggered-DiD efficient influence functions. The comparator studied here is deliberately narrower and different: a cohort-mean rank-one PPML-imputation estimator, with exact equivalence to Moreau--Kastler confined to the stated no-covariate, equal-weight aggregation boundary. Király, Theran, and Tomioka (2015) supply cycle algebra but no statistical tangent space. The precise delta is an if-and-only-if universal-efficiency theorem for the cohort-mean estimator: efficiency for every bounded legal covariance law holds exactly at cycle rank zero; at positive cycle rank, exactly \(q\) independent primitive covariance balances characterize the exceptional laws, and a support-preserving family realizes a positive-definite exact quadratic loss.
